text:
maria: Heads-up — we're onboarding Zephyr-11B-v2-xt for evals. License attached says 'non-commercial use only' and has a clause about 'redistribution of model weights prohibited'. Can we run quantized versions on Dedicated?
devon: quick Q — does our Dedicated offering count as redistribution if we host a quantized variant for a customer?
susan-legal: Short answer: depends on the license terms. 'Redistribution' often covers making copies available outside of upstream distribution channels. Hosting a model for a customer where they don't get the weights is usually allowed, but some licenses explicitly forbid "service" usage. Do you have the exact clause?
maria: Here's the excerpt we saw: "The Model may be used for evaluation and research. Commercial use, hosting as a service, or redistribution of underlying weights or converted formats is prohibited without a separate license."
jake: so hosting via Hosted API would be a no-go unless we have a commercial license. What about Dedicated/Private where customer controls VPC?
susan-legal: If the customer has a Private deployment (they run in their own infra and have the weights), that's often treated as distribution — you need permission to provide the weights. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs) we're effectively providing inference-as-service — that looks like hosting and thus falls under 'hosting as a service' prohibition.
amelia: Follow-up: we plan to ship int8 quantized weights for latency. Does converting architecture (quantization) count as a derivative that triggers redistribution rules?
susan-legal: Converting formats or quantizing can count as creating a derivative. If redistribution of derivatives is restricted, then distributing quantized weights or allowing download is blocked. Running quantized model in our closed infra for a customer still can be 'hosting' — license prohibits that.
devon: What about just running evals and benchmarks internally (no external access) and storing KV/prefix caches for faster reruns — any issue there?
susan-legal: Internal evaluation without external hosting is usually fine if license allows research/eval. But be cautious about storing user prompts or data in persistent caches that could be shared or exported. Also if the license has a clause forbidding use on data that includes proprietary corpora, check that too.
amelia: On the technical side: we keep a prefix cache that stores embeddings & tokenized prefixes to speed cold-starts. Is that considered 'storing model outputs' or user data?
jake: technote: prefix cache stores tokens + model internal KV snapshots, not weights. We don't expose them as a model artifact.
susan-legal: Storing model outputs or KV caches isn't the same as redistributing weights, but if the license forbids derivative artifacts that enable reuse/replication, there could be risk. Recommend we design cache retention policies and encrypt-at-rest.
maria: Action items: 1) engineering to add cache TTL + encryption; 2) legal to request a commercial license or explicit hosting waiver from Zephyr upstream; 3) product to flag Zephyr as 'HOSTING_BLOCKED' in model catalog until cleared. Agree?
ev-deploy-bot: deploy-bot: saved pinned note to onboarding checklist for Zephyr-11B-v2-xt :pushpin:
jake: I'll add a gating check in the model registry — block Dedicated/Hosted deployments until legal sign-off. Can we do evals on our test cluster without opening to customers?
susan-legal: Yes, internal-only evals are OK for now. If you surface any clauses about 'service prohibition' verbatim, share them and I'll draft an outreach email template to the upstream licensor.
amelia: For quant experiments, we'll run quantized inference in sandbox and record perf/quality but won't generate downloadable artifacts. We'll also log experiments (no user data).
maria: thanks — ping me once legal drafts the outreach. Also, add a note for support: if customers ask about licensing we should direct to sales/legal instead of promising hosting. :info:
